title: Two-Coordinate Expectation Under a Product Law
statement: Let $I$ and $A$ be finite types with decidable equality on $I$, and assign a probability law $\mu_i$ on $A$ to each $i\in I$. For distinct coordinates $j,k\in I$ and any function $F:A\times A\to\mathbb{R}$, its expectation on the pair of coordinates $(j,k)$ under the independent product law equals the iterated expectation of $F$ under $\mu_j$ and $\mu_k$.
hypotheses_covered: $I$ is a finite type with decidable equality
A probability law $\mu_i$ on $A$ is specified for each $i\in I$
Coordinates $j,k\in I$ are specified and distinct
